### J-1 Backslash in spec_says breaks the record title, leaving a half-done block
- quote: "f"Spec problem in {tid}: {str(cr['spec_says']).strip()}", by=by.strip())"
- situation (adversary): A handoff has `spec_says: "the path C:\data\new"`, or any text containing `\d`, `\q` or a trailing `\`. It passes the new line guard and the non-empty check. `records.new` puts the text unescaped (only `"` is escaped) into `title: "Spec problem in T-1: ...\d"`. That is invalid YAML. The sequence is: `shelve` runs and cleans the task's untracked files; the record is written; `records.parse(found)` raises `ValueError` and the command crashes; no `blocked` line is written, no waiting state is set, and the task is still `claimed` with its work shelved away; the broken `C-*.md` stays on disk, and every later `nio flow block` crashes in the lookup's `records.parse(p)`. `nio check` fails on the record as well. The failure is silent in the sense that the task looks claimed while its files are gone. It also breaks the memory check that FR-1 and AC-1 exist to protect.
- fix: Build the title from a single-line text with backslashes escaped as well as quotes. For example, reduce `spec_says` to one line and escape `\` before `"` in `records.new`. Alternatively, validate that the record parses before `shelve` and refuse the handoff otherwise. Add a test with a backslash in `spec_says`.
- validation: confirmed: The template (src/nio/templates/change.md:4) puts the title in a double-quoted YAML scalar, and records.new (records.py:289) escapes only `"`. A spec_says with `\d` or a trailing `\` therefore gives invalid YAML. In implement.block, the line guard (697) and the non-empty check (693) don't catch backslashes. `shelve` (710) has already run when `records.parse(found)` (721) raises ValueError, and the `blocked` line and waiting state are written only after that (722-725). The task is left claimed with its work shelved, and the broken C-*.md stays on disk. Later blocks then hit `records.parse(p)` in the lookup at 708 and crash.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-14

### J-2 Dead display labels in PARTS after the record body changed wording
- quote: "PARTS = (("spec_says", "What the spec says"), ("code_shows", "What the code shows"), ("smallest_change", "Smallest change"))"
- situation (consistency): the diff rewrites the record body to `The spec says: {...}` and `The code shows: {...}` under `## What is wrong`, and `{smallest_change}` under `## Proposed change`. The loops now read `for k, _ in PARTS`, so the names in the second element are never used for the record. A later edit that reads `PARTS` to build the body would get `What the spec says` and `Smallest change` headings, which are not the template's headings and contradict FR-2. The same tuple is also the only place the handoff keys are listed for validation.
- fix: keep `PARTS` as a tuple of keys only (e.g. `KEYS = ("spec_says", "code_shows", "smallest_change")`), with the validation loops over it, or drop the labels from `PARTS` and say in one comment that the record wording is hardcoded in `block`.

### J-3 Multi-line or backslash-ending spec_says reaches the record title unchecked
- quote: "f"Spec problem in {tid}: {str(cr['spec_says']).strip()}", by=by.strip())"
- situation (correctness): The guard checks each text for `## ` and `---` lines. `spec_says` is also put into the record's `title:` frontmatter by `records.new`, which only escapes `"`. If the text ends in a backslash, the title gets a `\"` and the YAML breaks. A multi-line `spec_says` makes a multi-line title. Either way the filed record can fail `nio check` even though the handoff was accepted, which is the failure FR-1 was meant to remove. This is an edge case and it existed before this change.
- fix: Collapse `spec_says` to one line and drop trailing backslashes before building the title, or refuse a handoff whose `spec_says` has a newline or backslash.
